keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Aram-Damascus (its Neo-Assyrian shapes cover the area from the annexation). The page gives no area and no boundary; it places the kingdom in southern Syria with Assyria to the north, Ammon to the south and Israel to the west, and says it 'reached most of the Golan'. The shape is the researcher's reading: the Damascus district (about 18,000 km2) plus the Golan (about 2,500 km2). Hazael's seizures in Israelite Transjordan and at Gath are carried as contests in the ledger, not as shape; Unqi was only an 'influence'.

ledger.note: c. 1100 BCE: the kingdom of Aram-Damascus arises at Damascus. The page says the polity 'existed from the late 12th century BCE to 732 BCE' (infobox 'Established: c. 12th century BCE'); it names no founder (the Rezon of 1 Kings is not on the page) and no founding act.

region.text: 'Israelite territory east of the Jordan River' that Hazael seized (Hazael page, citing 2 Kings 10:32-33)

ledger.note: 842 BCE (bridged): Hazael's wars take Israelite Transjordan. The Hazael page has him 'seized Israelite territory east of the Jordan River' (2 Kings 10:32-33) with no year; the Aram-Damascus page has him 'conquered Israel' 'in the 9th century BCE'; 842 is the first year of his reign ('Reign: 842-796 BC'). Mirrors the contest in the kingdom-of-israel dossier.

region.text: Gath (Tell es-Safi), 'the siege and subsequent conquest of Gath by Hazael'

ledger.note: c. 830 BCE (bridged): Hazael besieges and takes Gath. 'Recent excavations at Tell es-Safi/Gath have revealed dramatic evidence of the siege and subsequent conquest of Gath by Hazael' (undated on the page); the year mirrors the philistia dossier's c. 830, which rests on a page not opened here. Hazael's reign (842-796) bounds it.

wars.name: Battle of Qarqar and Shalmaneser III's campaigns against Damascus
wars.outcome: Assyrian claim of victory at Qarqar in 853 BC; 'Shalmaneser's opponents held on to their thrones after this battle' and the coalition's king Hadadezer remained king of Damascus until at least 841 BC. No border moved.
wars.note: The battle's date is 853 BC (a different eponym rescension gives 854). Hadadezer 'led' the coalition with 1,200 chariots, 1,200 horsemen and 20,000 soldiers; Irhuleni of Hamath, Ahab of Israel, Arqa, Ammon (Ba'asa), Quwe, Arwad, Usannata, Arabia (Gindibu) and others took part. The page says Shalmaneser engaged Hadadezer six times 'in the following decade' without naming years; the end year 842 is the infobox start of Hazael.

wars.outcome: Hazael 'seized Israelite territory east of the Jordan River', took Gath and 'sought to take Jerusalem' without success; Israel recovers after his death.
wars.note: All undated except by his reign (842-796 BC); the Tel Dan stele is 'seen by most scholars as having been erected by Hazael'. The Aram-Damascus page adds 'some influence over the northern Syrian state of Unqi' in the 9th century.

wars.name: Syro-Ephraimite War
wars.outcome: Rezin and Pekah's invasion of Judah (735 BCE) fails; Assyria annexes Aram-Damascus and 'much of Levant' by 732.
wars.note: The infobox gives 736-732 BCE, the body 735 for the invasion. The page dates neither Tiglath-Pileser's campaign nor the fall of Damascus.

certainty.note: No boundary of Aram-Damascus is described on any page opened; the southern edge with Ammon and the western edge with Israel are approximate.

notes: Cliopatria has no Aram-Damascus; the rows Neo-Assyrian Empire and Kingdom of Israel (me-02 and me-04-a) are the only Cliopatria trace. The Aram-Damascus infobox starts the kingdom 'c. 12th century BCE', but the page, the Aram-Zobah page and the Hazael page give no events before Ben-Hadad I (885 BCE), so the early life is a Damascus core and nothing more: David's overlordship over Aram-Zobah and Damascus (the kingdom-of-israel dossier has vassal_start -1000 and vassal_end -930 for 'aram-damascus') is not on any page opened here (the Aram-Zobah page says David 'defeated Zobah' and that 'Upon the accession of Solomon, Zobah became independent of Israel', undated). Aram-Zobah (Beqaa to Hama) has no dossier; its extent on that page is 'extended from the Beqaa Valley along the eastern side of the Anti-Lebanon Mountains', reaching 'Hama to the north and Damascus to the south', and it may be the same state in its early phase. Hazael's Transjordan seizure is drawn as a contest (matching the Israel dossier) although the page says 'seized' and 'conquered Israel'; a reviewer could instead call it a gain from 842 to 796. The Hazael page and the Aram-Damascus page do not date the Gath siege (the philistia dossier uses c. 830 from the Tell es-Safi page). The page budget of five pages was spent; a gap-filler should open 'Ben-Hadad I', 'Rezon' and 'Tiglath-Pileser III' for the 732 campaign and the Assyrian provinces of Damascus and Karnaim. The Hauran/Bashan are not drawn as Aramean because no page opened names them.
